text:
jamie: Heads-up — noticed CA is evicting a few GPU spot nodes in us-west2 even though there's queued pods; causes PDB flaps and model-serving latency spike. Anyone else seeing weird scaling when we mix preemptible+on-demand GPU nodegroups?
rachel: yeah saw that at 09:12 — scale-down removed a node with 3 small gpu pods that had local model cache. CA thought utilization low. logs: `scaleDownCandidates: []` then immediate delete?
omar: root cause might be PodTopologySpread + `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage` not set correctly. Those pods mark local storage so CA should skip but maybe our annotation missing.
tessa: we label spot nodes `preemptible=true` and taint `spot=true:NoSchedule`. Pods tolerate it but priority class low. CA uses binpacking and sometimes prefers evicting spot nodes — want to keep on-demand for latency-sensitive pods.
jamie: current CA flags on controllers: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 --expander=least-waste`. Thinking of `--expander=priority` + nodegroup priority weights. Also `--balance-similar-node-groups=true`?
omar: try to be careful with `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage` semantics — default is true (so CA skips nodes with local storage). We want CA to avoid removing nodes with cached models, so keep default true and ensure our pods expose `local-storage` ephemeral volumes correctly.
rachel: For preemptible mixing, we've had good luck with node-group priorities in CA v1.20+: set `--expander=priority` and annotate nodegroups with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority=100` for on-demand, 10 for spot. CA will prefer to scale down spot instead of on-demand.
kevin: Also look at `--max-empty-bulk-delete` and `--scale-down-delay-after-add` — if we scale-up aggressively and then CA immediately deletes because utilization drops that's churn. I recommend bumping `--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m`.
tessa: Another leaky point: Pods with `hostNetwork: true` (tf-serving) prevent eviction. CA may not see them as candidate but combination of PDB causing partial removal leaves degraded capacity. Suggest adding `preStop` hooks that checkpoint model cache so it's safe to move.
infra-bot: autoscaler: saw scale down event at 1728459850 - node pool gpu-spot-us-west2 removed (id: ng-spot-23) — 3 pods evicted
omar: Network limits: when many GPU nodes come up ENI/NAT quotas hit and kubelet can't register fast, CA thinks nodes are 'NotReady' and deletes others. We should stagger startup via `max-node-provision` or controller-side jitter. For cloud providers, ensure subnet IP quota is sufficient.
jamie: quick example annotation we plan to add to nodegroups:
```
cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority: "100"  # on-demand
cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority: "10"   # spot
```
Plan: 1) switch to `--expander=priority` and annotate NG priorities; 2) increase `--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m`; 3) enforce `podPriority` for latency-sensitive models so CA keeps on-demand; 4) add lifecycle hook to checkpoint local cache and improve startup jitter. I'll open infra PR and run canary in staging.
rachel: :thumbsup: I'll help with annotation and test in staging.
kevin: Also add metric alert on scale churn (>=3 scale events per 30m) + PDB violation rate.
